name: MAPS
question: Does therapist-led pelvic floor muscle training with indicated bladder training reduce persistent incontinence after radical prostatectomy or TURP compared with standard care?

design.blinding: Participants and therapists unmasked; outcome-data entry blinded

arms.label: Therapist-led pelvic floor muscle training with indicated bladder training

design.population: 853 men with urinary incontinence around six weeks after radical prostatectomy (411) or TURP (442) in 34 UK centres; mean time from surgery to randomisation was approximately eight weeks.
design.description: Two parallel UK multicentre randomized superiority trials
design.locator: Lancet accepted manuscript pp6–7,10, Table 1; HTA Chapter 2, Study design and populations

verdictNote: Neither trial showed a significant continence benefit; NHS costs increased without a QALY advantage.
takeaway: Four one-to-one therapist sessions of pelvic floor muscle training with indicated bladder training showed no statistically significant reduction in 12-month incontinence versus standard care after radical prostatectomy or TURP; both UK trials found higher NHS costs without a QALY advantage.

delivery.label: Therapist visits and technique
delivery.value: First 60-minute assessment followed by three approximately 45-minute visits at about 2, 6 and 12 weeks; digital anal examination provided verbal feedback on contractions.
delivery.locator: Full text, Chapter 2, Interventions, pp 10–11; Chapter 3, Summary of the MAPS intervention, p 28

delivery.label: Home program and urgency treatment
delivery.value: Three maximum-strength contractions in lying, sitting and standing positions twice daily, with 10-second breaks between contractions; a slight pelvic-floor lift while walking, contraction before leakage triggers and after voiding; urge suppression and bladder training for urgency.
delivery.locator: Full text, Chapter 3, Pelvic floor muscle training and Bladder training/urge suppression, pp 28–29

delivery.label: Machine-mediated biofeedback
delivery.value: Used in 17 men after radical prostatectomy and 10 after TURP across five centres; digital anal examination with verbal feedback was the standard intervention.
delivery.locator: Full text, Chapter 3, Biofeedback and Centres, resources and therapists, pp 28–29

results.note: Adjusted intention-to-treat RR; unadjusted risk difference 3.4 percentage points (95% CI −6 to 13). The trial was powered to detect a 15-point reduction; 194/220 and 203/222 randomized men supplied 12-month outcomes.

delivery.label: Index prostate procedures
delivery.value: Radical prostatectomy included abdominal, perineal and laparoscopic approaches, with no robotic procedures; TURP included standard and laser resections, with no HoLEP.
delivery.locator: Full text, Table 1 and footnotes, pp 19–20

delivery.label: Attendance at one or more therapist visits
delivery.value: 189/205 (92%) after radical prostatectomy and 189/220 (86%) after TURP; final visit attended by 175/205 (85%) and 158/220 (72%), respectively, without necessarily attending every interim visit.
delivery.locator: Full text, Results, Exercise behaviour and treatment compliance, p 9; Table 4, p 26

delivery.label: Usual-care context
delivery.value: All men received a lifestyle advice leaflet; control participants could receive routine non-specialist pelvic floor exercise information and other usual NHS care.
